      properties:

          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true

          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'

        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:

          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"

## Summary

I implemented the `riskFlag` field on the owner read model so it is `true` when any of the three risk signals hold, and `false` otherwise. Each piece of logic lives in its natural home:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added a `riskFlag` read-only boolean to the `Owner` schema (the DTO is generated from this spec), documenting the three conditions.

2. **`DisposableEmailRule`** (`rest/validation`) — This class already owns all disposable-email knowledge, so I added `isDisposableAdjacent(email)` there. It reuses the existing blocklist by deriving each blocked provider's second-level label (e.g. `mailinator`) once, and flags any email whose domain shares such a label — catching the same provider under a different TLD (`mailinator.net`) or as a subdomain (`mx.mailinator.com`) without being on the exact blocklist (exact disposables are already rejected at creation by `@NotDisposableEmail`). I also refactored the shared `@`-domain extraction into a `domainOf` helper so `isDisposable` and `isDisposableAdjacent` don't duplicate it.

3. **`OwnerMapper`** — Added a small `resolveRiskFlag(owner)` derivation alongside the other derived read-only fields (`ownerSegment`, `contactPreference`, etc.), wired via `@Mapping`. It ORs the three signals, each already exposed by the owner or the rule:
   - possible duplicate → `owner.isPossibleDuplicate()`
   - disposable-adjacent email → `DisposableEmailRule.isDisposableAdjacent(owner.getEmail())`
   - city over soft capacity → `owner.isCapacityWarning()` (the persisted 40–49 "approaching the 50 cap" snapshot, i.e. over the soft-capacity warning threshold)

I placed the aggregation in the mapper rather than the `Owner` entity to avoid a model→`rest.validation` layering dependency — the mapper already legitimately depends on the `rest.validation` resolvers and is where all the other derived read-only DTO fields are assembled.

One interpretation note: I mapped "over its soft capacity" to the owner's persisted `capacityWarning` (a creation-time snapshot), consistent with how `possibleDuplicate` is also a persisted signal. This keeps the mapper free of a repository dependency. If the intent was instead to reflect the city's *current* occupancy on each read, that would require threading the `ClinicService` into the read path — let me know and I can adjust.
